subject: reindeer herd
title: What If 29 Reindeer Landed on an Island With No Predators? 6,000, Then 42

scenes.text: What if 29 reindeer landed on an island with no wolves and no hunters? Paradise, for 19 years.
August 1944. The US Coast Guard shipped 29 reindeer to St. Matthew Island, Alaska, as emergency food for 19 men at a radio station. The men left first.
By 1957: 1,350, fat and healthy. By 1963: 6,000, or 47 per square mile, and already smaller than before.
The lichen they lived on was trampled flat. Then came the winter of 1963 to 64, one of the coldest and snowiest on record.
In 1966, a biologist counted 42: 41 females and one male that couldn't breed. No fawns. 99 percent gone in three years.
By the 1980s, there were none. An island with no predators isn't paradise. It's a bill that arrives all at once.

description:
What if reindeer were released on an island with no predators? In August 1944 the US Coast Guard put 29 on St. Matthew Island, Alaska, as a backup food supply for a 19-man navigation station, then withdrew the men.
Biologist David Klein counted 1,350 reindeer in 1957 and 6,000 in 1963, about 47 per square mile, with the lichen mats overgrazed. After the severe winter of 1963 to 64 he found 42 survivors in 1966, 41 females and one infertile male, a 99 percent crash; by the 1980s the herd was gone.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The island is 32 miles long and sits over 200 miles from the nearest village, so nobody saw the crash happen. Which population boom should we run through next?
